title: QEMU e2e tests: run asupersync unit test subset on ARM and RISC-V targets
description:
## Context
The current QEMU setup (bd-aw69.3) only validates that trivial "return 0" binaries
run. This is necessary but insufficient — it proves QEMU works, not that asupersync
works on embedded targets. We need to run actual asupersync operations under
emulation to prove functional correctness on ARM and RISC-V.

## IMPORTANT: Existing Linux-musl QEMU Infrastructure
tools/ci/run_qemu_smoke.sh (395 lines) already provides a COMPLETE QEMU user-mode
test harness for Linux-musl targets (mipsel/armv7/aarch64). It includes:
- qemu-*-static binary detection and execution
- JSONL logging, timeout handling, artifact collection, trace digest
- CLI: --build-first, --dry-run, --strict, --timeout, --target

This bead creates COMPLEMENTARY bare-metal QEMU semihosting tests (ARM Cortex-M,
RISC-V), NOT a replacement for run_qemu_smoke.sh. The existing harness tests
Linux-musl targets; this bead tests bare-metal targets with semihosting.

## Background
Running the full 64-suite test battery under bare-metal QEMU is impractical: the tests
use host-specific features (printf for test output, malloc for CORE profile tests, etc.).
Instead, we need a curated subset of tests that:
- Use only FREESTANDING or EMBEDDED_ROUTER profile APIs
- Don't require host stdio (use semihosting for minimal output)
- Don't depend on real timers or threading
- Exercise the critical path: region lifecycle, task scheduling, obligation tracking

## Task
1. Create tests/embedded/embedded_smoke.c — a self-contained test program that:
   a. Provides custom asx_runtime_hooks (static buffer allocator, no-op log_sink,
      monotonic counter as logical_clock)
   b. Opens a region, spawns tasks, runs scheduler, drains region
   c. Verifies task states, obligation states, quiescence
   d. Tests channel operations (EMBEDDED_ROUTER profile only, ifdef-guarded)
   e. Reports pass/fail via semihosting exit code (0 = pass, non-zero = fail count)
   f. Optionally emits minimal test log via semihosting SYS_WRITE0

2. Create tests/embedded/embedded_channel_smoke.c — channel-specific tests for
   EMBEDDED_ROUTER profile:
   a. Channel create, reserve, send, recv, close
   b. Backpressure (full channel returns correct error)
   c. Fairness (round-robin recv across multiple senders)

3. Create tools/ci/run_qemu_e2e.sh that:
   a. Cross-compiles embedded_smoke.c + libasx.a for each bare-metal target
   b. Runs under QEMU with semihosting (qemu-system-arm -semihosting, etc.)
   c. Captures exit code and semihosting output
   d. Reports per-target results with JSONL logging
   e. Runs EMBEDDED_ROUTER tests on targets that support it
   f. Uses same JSONL format conventions as existing run_qemu_smoke.sh for consistency

4. JSONL Log Format (consistent with run_qemu_smoke.sh):
   {"ts":"...","test":"embedded_smoke","target":"arm-m4-free","status":"pass","exit_code":0,"duration_ms":1200}
   {"ts":"...","test":"embedded_channel_smoke","target":"arm-m4-router","status":"pass","exit_code":0,"duration_ms":1800}

5. Test the test: create tests/embedded/test_hooks_minimal.c that unit-tests the
   custom hooks implementation (static allocator, counter clock) to ensure the test
   infrastructure itself is correct.

## Integration with Existing Infrastructure
- run_qemu_e2e.sh should REUSE tools/ci/run_qemu_baremetal.sh (from bd-aw69.3) for
  the actual QEMU semihosting invocation — do NOT duplicate QEMU launch logic
- run_qemu_e2e.sh handles: cross-compilation, test selection, result aggregation
- run_qemu_baremetal.sh handles: QEMU binary selection, semihosting flags, timeout, exit code capture
- Both scripts follow the same CLI conventions as run_qemu_smoke.sh
  (--dry-run, --strict, --timeout, --target)
- JSONL output should be compatible with the same log aggregation tooling
- The CI gate (bd-aw69.7) should run BOTH run_qemu_smoke.sh (Linux-musl) AND
  run_qemu_e2e.sh (bare-metal) for comprehensive coverage

## Static Allocator Design
The FREESTANDING profile needs a static buffer allocator for hooks:
- Pre-allocated uint8_t buffer[8192] (configurable)
- Bump allocator with alignment support
- realloc via copy-to-new-offset (no real realloc needed)
- free is a no-op (bump allocator doesn't reclaim)
- This is intentionally simple — good enough for test scenarios

## Acceptance Criteria
- embedded_smoke.c passes on all 4 FREESTANDING targets (arm-m4, arm-m0, riscv32, riscv64)
- embedded_channel_smoke.c passes on all 4 EMBEDDED_ROUTER targets
- All 8 test runs produce exit code 0 under QEMU semihosting
- JSONL log output compatible with existing run_qemu_smoke.sh format
- Static allocator is tested independently
- Test exercises at minimum: region open/close, task spawn/schedule/complete,
  obligation reserve/commit, quiescence check, cleanup callback

## Why This Matters
The existing run_qemu_smoke.sh validates Linux-musl targets, which still depend on
libc. Bare-metal semihosting tests prove that asupersync's FREESTANDING and
EMBEDDED_ROUTER profiles truly work without ANY OS or libc — the core value
proposition of the ANSI C port for embedded deployment.

title: [Epic] POSIX Platform Adapter
description:
Replace the empty src/platform/posix/hooks.c stub with a real POSIX platform adapter that populates asx_runtime_hooks for live-mode POSIX targets.

## Background
The asx runtime uses a composed hook family architecture (asx_runtime_hooks in include/asx/asx_config.h) with 5 categories: allocator, clock, entropy, reactor, log. Default implementations in src/runtime/hooks.c provide safe fallbacks (malloc, return-0 clock, counter PRNG, 0-event reactor, stderr log). Platform adapters override these defaults with real OS primitives.

Currently src/platform/posix/hooks.c is completely empty inside its #ifdef ASX_PROFILE_POSIX guard. This means anyone building with -DASX_PROFILE_POSIX gets zero platform integration — no real clock, no real entropy, no real reactor, no real threading.

## Scope
Wave B/C. The CORE profile (Wave A) works without this, but POSIX profile users need real hooks for live-mode operation.

## Deliverables
1. Clock hooks: clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC) for wall time, passthrough for logical time
2. Entropy hook: getrandom(2) with /dev/urandom fallback for seeded PRNG initialization
3. Reactor hook: epoll_create1/epoll_ctl/epoll_wait wrapper for the reactor.wait_fn
4. Blocking pool worker: pthread_create + condvar replacing inline execution
5. Export function: asx_posix_hooks_install(asx_runtime_hooks *h) as single entry point
6. Public header: include/asx/platform/posix.h declaring the install function
7. Unit tests: clock monotonicity, entropy distribution, reactor basic poll
8. Makefile: build-posix target with conditional PLATFORM_SRC and -lpthread linking
9. E2E smoke: tests/e2e/posix_adapter_smoke.sh exercising clock+entropy+reactor in a live scenario

## Hook signatures (from asx_config.h)
- allocator: malloc_fn(ctx, size), realloc_fn(ctx, ptr, size), free_fn(ctx, ptr)
- clock: now_ns_fn(ctx) -> asx_time, logical_now_ns_fn(ctx) -> asx_time
- entropy: random_u64_fn(ctx) -> uint64_t
- reactor: wait_fn(ctx, timeout_ms, ready_count), ghost_wait_fn(ctx, logical_step, ready_count)
- log: write_fn(ctx, level, message)

## Files
- src/platform/posix/hooks.c (modify: replace empty stub)
- include/asx/platform/posix.h (new: public declaration)
- Makefile (modify: add build-posix target)
- tests/unit/platform/test_posix_hooks.c (new: unit tests)
- tests/e2e/posix_adapter_smoke.sh (new: e2e smoke)
close_reason: All 9 deliverables complete: clock hooks, entropy hook, reactor (epoll+poll), blocking pool (pthread), install function, public header, unit tests (12 passing), Makefile build-posix target, E2E smoke test (7/7 scenarios). Header comment updated.

title: CLI: implement main.c with doctor, info, and version subcommands
description:
## Deliverable
Create src/cli/main.c — a standalone CLI entry point that links against libasx.a and provides:

### Relationship to existing cli.c
src/cli/cli.c (158 lines) already exists and provides LIBRARY UTILITY functions (output format parsing, flag helpers, etc). These are part of libasx.a.

The NEW main.c is a SEPARATE standalone entry point that USES the existing cli.c utilities. It is NOT compiled into libasx.a — it only links against it. This separation means:
- cli.c stays in the library as utility functions
- main.c is a standalone program that links libasx.a

### `asx version`
Print: asx <version> (profile=<PROFILE> codec=<CODEC> det=<0|1>)
Use asx_version_string() if available, or construct from compile-time macros.

### `asx info`
Print:
- Active profile name and ID (via asx_profile_active() / asx_profile_name())
- Resource class (R1/R2/R3) with limits table (via asx_profile_resource_config())
- Number of ASX_API declarations (compile-time constant)
- Compile-time flags (ASX_PROFILE_*, ASX_CODEC_*, ASX_DETERMINISTIC)
- Available surfaces (via asx_surface_gate() for each surface)

### `asx doctor`
Run diagnostic checks using existing app/doctor.c APIs:
- Verify hooks are installed and validate (asx_runtime_hooks_validate)
- Check clock monotonicity (call now_ns twice, verify non-decreasing)
- Check entropy (generate 10 samples, verify variance)
- Check allocator (malloc/free a small buffer)
- Report pass/fail for each check with descriptive names
- Support --format json for structured output (use asx_cli_parse_output_format from cli.c)
- Return exit code 0 if all pass, 1 otherwise

### Argument parsing
Simple hand-rolled parsing (no getopt dependency for freestanding compat):
- `asx` with no args → print usage summary
- `asx version` → version info
- `asx info` → profile/capability info
- `asx doctor [--format text|json]` → run diagnostics
- `asx help` / `asx --help` / `asx -h` → full usage
- Unknown subcommand → error message + usage, exit 1

### Makefile integration
Add to Makefile:
```make
CLI_BIN := build/bin/asx

cli: $(LIB_A) src/cli/main.c | build/bin
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -o $(CLI_BIN) src/cli/main.c $(LIB_A) $(LDFLAGS)

build/bin:
	mkdir -p build/bin
```
Also add `cli` to the .PHONY list and optionally to `make install` (install the binary alongside the library).

### Error handling
All subcommands must handle initialization failures gracefully:
- If asx_runtime_hooks_init fails, print error and exit 1
- If profile detection fails, print 'unknown profile' rather than crashing

## Files
- src/cli/main.c (new: ~200-300 lines)
- Makefile (modify: add cli target, build/bin directory)

title: Child regions: Enforce parent-waits-for-children in drain
description:
Modify the drain/finalize path so that a parent region cannot advance past CLOSING while it has live (non-CLOSED) children.

## Current behavior
The drain path in quiescence.c (around line 215) advances regions through CLOSING → DRAINING → FINALIZING → CLOSED. Currently it skips DRAINING ("no children (walking skeleton) — fast path").

## New behavior
Before advancing past CLOSING:
1. Check r->child_count > 0
2. If yes: stay in CLOSING, return ASX_E_PENDING (children must close first)
3. If no: proceed to DRAINING as before

This ensures the parent region lifecycle respects the child region hierarchy. Children must be explicitly closed before parent can finalize.

## Files
- src/runtime/quiescence.c (modify: drain advancement logic)

title: Child regions: Track child close and decrement parent child_count
description:
When a child region transitions to CLOSED state, decrement the parent's child_count and remove the child from the parent's children[] array.

In src/runtime/lifecycle.c, find where region state becomes CLOSED (likely in the drain/finalize path in quiescence.c or lifecycle.c). Add:
1. If region->parent_id != ASX_INVALID_ID: look up parent slot
2. Scan parent->children[] for this region's id
3. Remove it (shift remaining entries or swap with last)
4. Decrement parent->child_count
5. Handle edge case: parent already closed/freed — log warning but don't crash

## Idempotency
Must be safe if called multiple times (e.g., if close path runs twice due to error recovery). Check child is actually in parent's list before decrementing.

## What to implement

Use __has_include or check for SYS_getrandom. On macOS, use getentropy() from <sys/random.h>. The fallback path (/dev/urandom) works everywhere.

- Verify no errors returned (getrandom should not fail with 8 bytes)
- Guard test with #ifdef ASX_PROFILE_POSIX

title: EPIC: Hardcoded Constants, Stale Comments, and Code Quality Remediation
description:
Master epic for systematically addressing all hardcoded magic numbers that should be configurable,
stale/misleading comments indicating unfinished code, and related code quality issues discovered
during a comprehensive fresh-eyes audit of the entire asupersync ANSI C codebase.

## Background

A full-project audit was conducted scanning every .c and .h file for:
1. Hardcoded numeric constants in function bodies that should be named #define macros
2. Comments containing "will", "would", "TODO", "FIXME" indicating unfinished or deferred work
3. Stale documentation that no longer matches the actual implementation state

## Scope

This epic covers:
- Converting 4 hardcoded magic numbers to named, #ifndef-guarded compile-time constants
- Updating 2 stale header comments that incorrectly describe code as stubs/future work
- Identifying and documenting items verified as correct (not needing changes)
- Ensuring all changes compile cleanly with -Werror and pass existing test suites

## Architectural Principle

The asx project uses a "resource contracts instead of silent degradation" philosophy (README).
Every operational parameter should be:
1. Named (self-documenting in code)
2. Overridable at compile time (#ifndef guard)
3. Documented with its default value and unit
4. Consistent with the profile/resource-class system

This ensures embedded deployers (R1/R2/R3 resource classes) and specialized profiles
(HFT, AUTOMOTIVE) can tune thresholds without modifying source code.

## Verification

All changes MUST:
- Build cleanly with `make build` (strict -Werror)
- Pass all existing unit tests
- Not change any runtime behavior when using default values
- Be backward-compatible (existing code that doesn't override the macros gets identical behavior)
close_reason: All tasks completed: 4 constants extracted, 2 comments fixed, audit trail documented

title: SUB-EPIC: Hardcoded Magic Numbers → Named Compile-Time Constants
description:
Convert all hardcoded magic numbers in function bodies to named #define macros with
#ifndef guards, enabling compile-time override by deployers.

## Why This Matters

The asx project targets 9 deployment profiles (CORE through BROWSER) and 3 resource
classes (R1/R2/R3). Each profile has different operational envelopes. Hardcoded constants
prevent deployers from tuning behavior without source modification, violating the
"resource contracts instead of silent degradation" principle.

## Pattern

For each constant:
1. Add `#ifndef ASX_<MODULE>_<NAME>` / `#define` / `#endif` in the relevant public header
2. Replace the literal in the .c file with the macro name
3. Update any doc comments referencing the old literal value
4. Verify the default value matches the original literal exactly (zero behavior change)

## Constants Identified

| Constant | File | Value | Unit | New Macro |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Process wait poll guard | process.c:235 | 10000 | polls | ASX_PROCESS_WAIT_MAX_POLLS |
| App default poll budget | app.c:125 | 10000 | polls | ASX_APP_DEFAULT_POLL_BUDGET |
| HFT p99 gate threshold | hft_instrument.c:281 | 10000 | nanoseconds | ASX_HFT_DEFAULT_P99_NS |
| Automotive watchdog period | automotive_instrument.c:250,258 | 10000000 | nanoseconds | ASX_AUTO_DEFAULT_WATCHDOG_PERIOD_NS |

## Items Audited and Verified as Correct (No Change Needed)

These were examined and confirmed to be intentionally placed:
- hooks.c:62 `return 0` — Intentional platform hook stub; overridden at runtime init
- lab.c:57,93 `1000000ULL` tick_ns — Default in config struct; already user-configurable via asx_lab_config
- console.c:84 "would check isatty()" — Design note explaining platform-specific behavior
- plan.c:413 "this would set up a deadline" — Explaining deterministic simulation vs real async
- Profile overload thresholds (90/85/80/75%) in overload_catalog.c — Intentional per-profile policy
- Seqlock spike retry limits (100, 1000) — Experimental research code, not production path
close_reason: All 4 hardcoded constants extracted to named #ifndef-guarded macros

title: Extract ASX_PROCESS_WAIT_MAX_POLLS from process.c:235
description:
## What

Replace the hardcoded `10000u` poll guard in asx_process_wait_with_output() with a named
compile-time constant ASX_PROCESS_WAIT_MAX_POLLS.

## Where

- Header: include/asx/process/process.h (add #ifndef/#define/#endif block)
- Source: src/process/process.c line 235 (replace literal with macro)

## Why

asx_process_wait_with_output() polls in a bounded loop to prevent infinite hangs when
waiting for a child process to exit. The 10,000 iteration limit was chosen as a reasonable
default, but embedded deployers on slow hardware may need more iterations, while
latency-sensitive HFT profiles may want fewer.

Without a named constant, the only way to change this is to edit source code directly,
which violates the profile/resource-class customization model.

## Implementation

```c
// In process.h, after ASX_PROCESS_PROGRAM_MAX:
#ifndef ASX_PROCESS_WAIT_MAX_POLLS
#define ASX_PROCESS_WAIT_MAX_POLLS 10000u
#endif

// In process.c:235:
uint32_t max_polls = ASX_PROCESS_WAIT_MAX_POLLS;
```

## Verification

- `make build` passes with -Werror
- All process-related tests pass
- Default behavior unchanged (10000 iterations when macro not overridden)

## Status: COMPLETED

This task has been implemented and verified.

title: Extract ASX_APP_DEFAULT_POLL_BUDGET from app.c:125
description:
## What

Replace the hardcoded `10000` default poll budget in asx_app_init() with a named
compile-time constant ASX_APP_DEFAULT_POLL_BUDGET.

## Where

- Header: include/asx/app/app.h (add #ifndef/#define/#endif before asx_app_config typedef)
- Source: src/app/app.c line 125 (replace literal with macro)
- Doc comment: app.h line 75 updated from "0 = 10000" to "0 = ASX_APP_DEFAULT_POLL_BUDGET"

## Why

When a user creates an asx_app_config with poll_budget=0, the app framework defaults to
10,000 polls per run. This default is reasonable for general-purpose CORE profile, but:
- Embedded router (R1) deployments may want 1,000 to conserve cycles
- HFT profiles may want 100,000 for uninterrupted processing bursts
- Testing scenarios may want very small budgets (64) for deterministic control

The asx_app_config struct already has the poll_budget field, but the fallback default
was a bare literal. Now it's a named macro that deployers can override.

## Implementation

```c
// In app.h, before asx_app_config:
#ifndef ASX_APP_DEFAULT_POLL_BUDGET
#define ASX_APP_DEFAULT_POLL_BUDGET 10000u
#endif

// In app.c:125:
if (app->config.poll_budget == 0) { app->config.poll_budget = ASX_APP_DEFAULT_POLL_BUDGET; }
```

## Verification

- `make build` passes with -Werror
- App-related tests pass (test_app.c, though currently blocked by surface gating in CORE profile)
- Default behavior unchanged

## Status: COMPLETED

title: Extract ASX_HFT_DEFAULT_P99_NS from hft_instrument.c:281
description:
## What

Replace the hardcoded `10000` (10 microsecond) p99 latency gate threshold in
asx_hft_gate_init() with a named compile-time constant ASX_HFT_DEFAULT_P99_NS.

## Where

- Header: include/asx/runtime/hft_instrument.h (add before asx_hft_gate typedef)
- Source: src/runtime/hft_instrument.c line 281 (replace literal with macro)

## Why

The HFT metric gate evaluates whether runtime latency meets trading-floor requirements.
The p99 threshold of 10µs is a reasonable default for modern hardware, but:
- Co-located exchange servers may need 1µs (1000ns)
- Remote-feed processors may tolerate 100µs (100000ns)
- Lab/testing environments may want no gate (UINT64_MAX)

The HFT profile's whole purpose is tail-latency governance. Making the gate threshold
a hardcoded literal defeats the profile's customizability.

## Design Note

The gate struct already has p99_ns as a runtime field (users can set it after init).
The #define provides a compile-time default for the init function. Both customization
paths now work: compile-time via -DASX_HFT_DEFAULT_P99_NS=5000 and runtime via
direct struct assignment after asx_hft_gate_init().

## Implementation

```c
// In hft_instrument.h:
#ifndef ASX_HFT_DEFAULT_P99_NS
#define ASX_HFT_DEFAULT_P99_NS 10000u  /* 10 microseconds */
#endif

// In hft_instrument.c:281:
gate->p99_ns = ASX_HFT_DEFAULT_P99_NS;
```

## Status: COMPLETED

title: Extract ASX_AUTO_DEFAULT_WATCHDOG_PERIOD_NS from automotive_instrument.c:250,258
description:
## What

Replace the hardcoded `10000000u` (10ms) watchdog period in automotive_instrument.c
with a named compile-time constant ASX_AUTO_DEFAULT_WATCHDOG_PERIOD_NS. This literal
appeared in TWO locations: ensure_auto_init() and asx_auto_instrument_reset().

## Where

- Header: include/asx/runtime/automotive_instrument.h (add before Watchdog monitor section)
- Source: src/runtime/automotive_instrument.c lines 250 and 258 (both replaced)

## Why

The automotive watchdog monitors checkpoint intervals for safety-critical systems.
If a monitored entity goes longer than the watchdog period without checkpointing,
a violation is recorded. The 10ms default is appropriate for typical automotive ECUs,
but:
- Fast-cycle control loops (engine management) may need 1ms (1000000ns)
- Slow-cycle monitoring (climate control) may use 100ms (100000000ns)
- Functional safety standards (ISO 26262) may mandate specific intervals

The automotive profile exists specifically for this kind of safety-tuning.
Hardcoding the watchdog period undermines the profile's purpose.

## Two-Site Fix

The literal appeared in both ensure_auto_init() and asx_auto_instrument_reset().
Both MUST use the same macro to ensure reset restores the same default as initial
construction. Using different values would create a subtle behavior difference
between first-init and post-reset states.

## Implementation

```c
// In automotive_instrument.h:
#ifndef ASX_AUTO_DEFAULT_WATCHDOG_PERIOD_NS
#define ASX_AUTO_DEFAULT_WATCHDOG_PERIOD_NS 10000000u
#endif

// In automotive_instrument.c (both sites):
asx_auto_watchdog_init(&g_watchdog, ASX_AUTO_DEFAULT_WATCHDOG_PERIOD_NS);
```

## Status: COMPLETED

title: SUB-EPIC: Stale Comments and Misleading Documentation
description:
Fix header comments and doc strings that no longer accurately describe the implementation.
Stale comments are particularly dangerous in a safety-oriented codebase because they mislead
future developers about the actual state of the code.

## Why This Matters

The asx codebase is designed for deterministic replay, formal verification, and
cross-profile parity. When a header says "stubs will be replaced" but the implementation
is fully functional, a developer may:
- Skip integration because they think the feature isn't available
- Add redundant fallback logic for a "missing" feature that actually works
- File false bug reports about stub behavior

## Comments Identified

1. raptorq.h — Header claims "fail-closed stub" but encode/decode ARE implemented with XOR erasure coding
2. parallel.h — Says "Real multi-threaded dispatch will be added when..." (future-tense promise)

## Items Verified as Acceptable (Design Notes, Not Stale)

These use "would" or "will" but are legitimate documentation:
- io_adapter.h: "would block, waker will be signaled" — Describes async contract semantics
- stream.h: "would block" / "will be signaled" — Same pattern, standard async documentation
- pool.h: "will be destroyed when returned" — Documents lifecycle contract
- transport.h: "would block, try again later" — Standard non-blocking I/O documentation
- runtime.h: "poll_fn will be called by the scheduler" — Documents callback contract
- automotive_instrument.h: "would trigger at the given time" — Conditional query documentation
close_reason: Both stale header comments updated to match actual implementation

title: Fix stale raptorq.h header: claims stub but encode/decode are implemented
description:
## What

Update the raptorq.h header comment from "fail-closed stub" / "stubs will be replaced"
to accurately describe the current XOR-based erasure coding implementation.

## Where

- Header: include/asx/raptorq/raptorq.h lines 1-20

## Before (Stale)

```c
/* asx/raptorq/raptorq.h — RaptorQ erasure coding surface (fail-closed stub)
 *
 * RaptorQ (RFC 6330) fountain erasure coding is exported by the upstream
 * Rust crate but is explicitly deferred in the ANSI C port per DEF-009
 * (Wave D, ~18k LOC equivalent, specialized audience).
 *
 * This header provides:
 *   - Configuration types that document the upstream contract
 *   - A readiness probe that returns ASX_E_NOT_FOUND (fail-closed)
 *   - String constants for diagnostic/interop messages
 *
 * When the full implementation lands, these stubs will be replaced by
 * real encode/decode/recover APIs.
```

## After (Accurate)

```c
/* asx/raptorq/raptorq.h — RaptorQ erasure coding surface
 *
 * Provides XOR-based erasure coding for symbol recovery. Encodes
 * source data into repair symbols that enable reconstruction when
 * some symbols are lost. Configuration controls symbol size, count,
 * and repair overhead.
 *
 * Upstream Rust parity: RaptorQConfig, encode, decode.
```

## Why This Mattered

The header was written when raptorq was a stub. The implementation was later replaced
with real XOR-based erasure coding (asx_raptorq_encode and asx_raptorq_decode in
src/raptorq/raptorq.c), but the header comment was never updated. This could cause:
- Developers skipping integration because they think it's a stub
- Confusion during code review ("why does the header say stub but the code works?")
- False bug reports about expected stub behavior

The migration.c feature table already lists raptorq as available=1, so the rest of
the codebase knows it's real — only the header comment was wrong.

## Status: COMPLETED

title: Fix stale parallel.h header: remove future-tense 'will be added' promise
description:
## What

Update the parallel.h header comment from "Real multi-threaded dispatch will be added
when platform threading hooks are implemented" to a factual present-tense description.

## Where

- Header: include/asx/runtime/parallel.h lines 8-10

## Before (Stale)

```c
 * Walking skeleton: single-threaded simulation of lane scheduling.
 * Real multi-threaded dispatch will be added when platform threading
 * hooks are implemented.
```

## After (Factual)

```c
 * Currently provides single-threaded lane scheduling simulation.
 * Multi-threaded dispatch requires platform threading hooks.
```

## Why

The original comment made a promise about future work ("will be added when...").
This is problematic because:
1. It implies someone is actively working on threading (they may not be)
2. It doesn't say WHAT the current code actually does (walking skeleton simulation)
3. Future-tense promises in code comments become stale the moment the developer moves on

The fix changes to present-tense factual description: here's what it does now,
here's what's needed to go further. No promises about when or if.

## General Principle

Comments should describe WHAT IS, not WHAT WILL BE. If something is planned,
track it in beads (the issue tracker), not in code comments. Comments that say
"will" or "TODO" are essentially invisible issue tickets with no assignee,
no priority, and no dependency tracking.

## Status: COMPLETED

title: Audit record: constants and comments verified as correct (no change needed)
description:
## Purpose

This bead documents items that were examined during the audit and explicitly determined
to NOT need changes. This prevents future auditors from re-investigating the same items.

## Hardcoded Values Verified as Intentionally Correct

### 1. hooks.c:62 — default_wall_clock returns 0
- **Value**: `return 0;`
- **Why correct**: This is an intentional platform hook stub. The walking skeleton runtime
  provides default hooks that are replaced at runtime init. The wall_clock hook returns 0
  because deterministic mode doesn't need real time, and non-deterministic deployments
  MUST register a real clock hook via asx_runtime_hooks_init(). Returning 0 is fail-safe:
  it makes time-dependent logic behave deterministically rather than using garbage values.

### 2. lab.c:57,93 — tick_ns defaults to 1000000 (1ms)
- **Value**: `cfg->tick_ns = 1000000ULL;`
- **Why correct**: This IS a configurable default — it's set in the asx_lab_config struct
  which users fill before calling asx_lab_init(). The literal appears in config_init (setting
  the default) and in lab_init (fallback if user left it 0). Users override it by setting
  cfg.tick_ns before init. No #define needed because the config struct IS the override mechanism.

### 3. console.c:84 — "would check isatty()"
- **Value**: Comment explaining platform-specific behavior
- **Why correct**: The comment says "A real platform adapter would check isatty() and TERM
  environment variable." This is a design note explaining what the platform hook should do,
  not a promise of future work. The CORE profile doesn't have terminal awareness by design.

### 4. plan.c:413 — "this would set up a deadline"
- **Value**: Comment explaining async vs deterministic behavior
- **Why correct**: The comment says "In a real async runtime, this would set up a deadline."
  This explains that the deterministic walking skeleton doesn't use real deadlines, which
  is the intended behavior for CORE profile. Not stale — it's architecture documentation.

title: [Epic] Child Region Tracking and Q2 Quiescence Fix
description:
Fix the only semantic contract violation in the walking skeleton: the Q2 quiescence conjunct (child regions closed) is hardcoded to 1 at src/runtime/quiescence.c:150 without actually checking.

## Background
The quiescence contract (docs/QUIESCENCE_FINALIZATION_INVARIANTS.md) requires four conjuncts:
- Q1: all tasks complete (implemented: checks r->task_count)
- Q2: all child regions closed (HARDCODED TO 1 — THIS IS THE BUG)
- Q3: all obligations resolved (implemented: checks obligations_reserved)
- Q4: cleanup stack drained (implemented: checks cleanup_drained)

The current code at quiescence.c line 150:
    /* Q2: all child regions closed (walking skeleton: always true) */
    out->q2_children_closed = 1;

This means any parent region with open child regions will incorrectly report as quiescent. The fix requires implementing a parent-child region model.

## Architecture
asx_region_slot (src/runtime/runtime_internal.h) currently has: state, task_count, task_total, generation, alive, poisoned, cleanup, capture_arena, capture_used. We need to add: parent_id, child_count, children[N].

The existing asx_region_open() creates root regions. We add asx_region_open_child(parent, &child) for hierarchical regions.

## Scope
Wave A — Critical. This is the only false assertion in the quiescence contract.

## Deliverables
1. Extended region slot struct with parent/child tracking
2. New asx_region_open_child() public API
3. Child close tracking (decrement parent's child_count on child CLOSED)
4. Real Q2 check: (r->child_count == 0) replaces hardcoded 1
5. Parent-waits-for-children drain enforcement
6. Comprehensive unit tests (parent/child lifecycle, Q2 verification, drain blocking)
7. CBMC harness for parent-child transition safety
8. E2E scenario exercising nested region lifecycle

## Risk
Touching runtime_internal.h affects sizeof(asx_region_slot) which affects static arena sizing. Must verify ASX_MAX_REGIONS * sizeof(new_slot) stays within acceptable BSS limits. children[8] adds 8*4=32 bytes + parent_id(4) + child_count(4) = 40 bytes per slot. With ASX_MAX_REGIONS=32, that's 1.25KB additional BSS.

## Files
- src/runtime/runtime_internal.h (modify: extend asx_region_slot)
- include/asx/asx_config.h (modify: add ASX_MAX_REGION_CHILDREN)
- include/asx/runtime/runtime.h (modify: add asx_region_open_child decl)
- src/runtime/lifecycle.c (modify: child open/close tracking)
- src/runtime/quiescence.c (modify: Q2 check, drain enforcement)
- tests/unit/runtime/test_quiescence.c (modify: add child region tests)
- tests/formal/cbmc/child_region_harness.c (new: CBMC harness)
- tests/e2e/e2e_nested_regions.c (new: e2e scenario)

title: Oracle increment 3b: race with deadline (scope.timeout wrapper task), first_ok, QuorumError mapping, GenServer actors, supervision
description:
Remaining DSL v2 steps neither oracle interprets (both fail closed by name), blocking 3 of 29 scenarios (combinators-race-timeout-001, actor-counter-cast-call-001, supervision-transient-restart-001):
- race deadline_ns: Rust runs the race inside cx.scope().timeout(&cx, d, op) (cx/scope.rs:2130), which SPAWNS the operation as its own task and, on the deadline, aborts it with CancelReason::timeout() and joins it; the race members are that task's children. C has no task-spawning timeout combinator (asx_task_group_set_deadline cancels members directly with TIMEOUT). Port Scope::timeout to C (or model it in the interpreter with a one-member group over a wrapper task) and add a vocabulary §2 name for the wrapper task. Note CancelReason::timeout() uses testing-default attribution (same class as bd-wxep).
- first_ok: cx.scope().first_ok (scope.rs:2023) vs C FIRST_OK.
- QuorumError (InsufficientSuccesses/Cancelled/Panicked/InvalidQuorum): vocabulary §5 mapping + C result parity (C returns the most severe member status).
- GenServer: Rust traces ~20 'gen_server::*' messages (gen_server.rs:668-1375) and uses mpsc reserve (SendPermit) + oneshot reply obligations; C asx_actor_* must reproduce the observable trace/obligation behaviour.
- supervision: SupervisorBuilder...spawn (supervision.rs) vs asx_supervisor_start; restart events/outcomes.
Known C divergences to expect (from task_group.h): same-round race ties go to the lowest index in C, to cx.random_usize in Rust; owner-cancel drains members with ParentCancelled in C vs the owner's own reason in Rust; quorum drain uses RaceLost in C vs CancelReason::quorum_met() in Rust.

comments.text: Semantic drift found (2026-10-09): Rust's Scope::first_ok (cx/scope.rs:2023-2099) is SEQUENTIAL: it spawns attempt i (spawn_in_cancellation_dominant), joins it to termination, returns on Ok, continues on Err, and stops with the failure list on Cancelled/Panicked/spawn refusal; it checks the caller's cancellation before each attempt and forwards it once to the attempt in flight (abort_with_reason with the caller's reason, then keeps joining). C's ASX_TASK_GROUP_FIRST_OK runs all members concurrently (they are spawned by the caller before asx_task_group_add) and drains the losers with RACE_LOST. Porting needs the group to own member factories (poll_fn + user_data) and spawn them one at a time, so it is an API change to asx_task_group, not a mode tweak. The FirstOkError result (all failures in order) also needs a vocabulary §5 mapping.

title: [Epic] RaptorQ Erasure Decode with Symbol Recovery
description:
Implement actual erasure recovery in asx_raptorq_decode(). Currently, the decode function at src/raptorq/raptorq.c:120-127 just memcpy's all received symbols without any recovery from lost symbols:

    /* Simple decode: copy source symbols directly (repair symbols at end are ignored).
     * Full recovery from symbol loss would require the repair XOR equations. */
    memcpy(dst, syms, copy_len);

The encode side (lines 82-94) already generates real XOR repair symbols using the pattern: repair[j] = XOR of source symbols where (i + j) % r == 0. The decoder must invert these equations.

## Background
The RaptorQ module (src/raptorq/raptorq.c) implements a simplified XOR-based erasure code (not RFC 6330 compliant). It provides encode/decode for the asx codec surface. The encoder works correctly — it generates k source symbols + r repair symbols. But the decoder ignores repair symbols entirely, meaning any symbol loss results in data corruption.

## Algorithm
The XOR peeling decoder:
1. Build an equation matrix: each repair symbol covers a known set of source symbols
2. Iterative peeling: find any equation with exactly 1 unknown source symbol, solve it (XOR repair with known sources)
3. Repeat until all source symbols are recovered or no single-unknown equations remain
4. If stuck: declare unrecoverable (ASX_E_RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED)

## Scope
Wave A. The encode is real; the decode must match.

## Deliverables
1. New asx_raptorq_decode_with_erasures() API taking symbol_present bitmap
2. XOR peeling solver implementation
3. Decodability rank check (fail early if too many losses)
4. Updated existing decode to fast-path when all symbols present
5. Unit tests: no-loss, single-loss, max-recoverable, unrecoverable
6. E2E erasure recovery test with detailed logging
7. Conformance test vectors with known erasure patterns

## Files
- include/asx/raptorq/raptorq.h (modify: add new decode API)
- src/raptorq/raptorq.c (modify: implement recovery)
- tests/unit/raptorq/test_raptorq.c (modify: add erasure tests)
- tests/e2e/e2e_raptorq_erasure.c (new: e2e erasure scenario)
close_reason: All RaptorQ tasks complete: API (bd-yf9u), XOR peeling solver (bd-1fsi), rank check (bd-3nny), unit tests (bd-zt9e), E2E scenario (bd-rwax). The simplified XOR erasure decoder recovers from single-symbol losses; multi-symbol recovery is limited by the peeling-only approach (documented in E2E test). Evidence: tests/unit/raptorq/test_raptorq.c, tests/e2e/e2e_raptorq_erasure.c. Artifact evidence: build/e2e/

title: Real Rust-vs-C differential fuzzing over DSL v2: twin_run generate + capture + asx-conformance compare + delta-debug minimizer
description:
Why: the 'Differential fuzzing gate (Rust vs C + minimized counterexamples)' required by AGENTS.md is not real. tests/fuzz/fuzz_differential.c compares against Rust only with --rust-binary (never passed by make/CI; 1717066 made the summary say 'skipped' instead of an unmeasured 0), and even then it compares two independently defined digests over different projections (tools/rust_fuzz_target: 'the digest may differ from C ... that difference IS the signal'), with divergences 'informational, not failures'.

The DSL v2 oracle (twin_run + asx-conformance, 25/26 fixtures matching at 3878d76) makes a real one cheap:
1. twin_run generate --seed S --count N --out DIR: seeded random asx.scenario.v2 documents over the interpreted step set (regions, tasks, yield/sleep/checkpoint/trace, obligations, spawn/join, masked, mpsc/oneshot/broadcast/watch, mutex/semaphore/barrier/notify, race/join_all/quorum, driver cancel_task/cancel_region/advance), bounded by lab.max_steps so deadlocks end deterministically (both engines must then agree on the non-quiescent snapshot).
2. twin_run capture on the batch; asx-conformance compare on the fixtures; every FAIL is a candidate drift.
3. Minimizer: delta-debug a failing scenario (drop tasks, steps, script entries) re-running both engines until 1-minimal; store minimized counterexamples under fixtures/fuzz_counterexamples_v2 with the Rust capture.
4. make fuzz-differential runs a small fixed-seed batch in CI (blocking on any non-allowlisted FAIL); a nightly larger batch.
Acceptance: a CI lane runs >= 200 generated scenarios per push through both engines; a planted C semantic mutation (e.g. FIFO grant order reversed in semaphore) is caught and minimized; known classified deltas (bd-wxep) are allowlisted by scenario hash, never by blanket skip. Retire the old --rust-binary digest path once this lands.

comments.text: First real run (seed 1, 100 generated scenarios; Rust captured 92): 48 divergences initially. Fixed: (1) oracle defect - twin_run named timers by reusable timer id (17 divergences); (2) C: cancelled holder's unresolved obligations were aborted Cancel, Rust leaks them (token drop); (3) C: cx.spawn-style children that acknowledged a post-first-poll cancel keep their value (Rust PreserveAcknowledgedCancellationResult); (4) C: asx_cx_checkpoint now acknowledges and observes budget deadline like Rust Cx::checkpoint; (5) C: poll quota charged before the poll + checkpoint observes poll_quota==0 (Rust consume-at-poll-start + checkpoint_budget_exhaustion); (6) C: a child spawned in its spawner's region inherits the spawner's current budget (Cx::inherited_budget). Now 69/92 match. Remaining classes (23): A) Rust leaves sleep timers pending when a sleep completes after an explicit driver advance without its timer firing (lab stops at quiescence; C fires them) e.g. gen-1-17/34/37/49/59; B) timer.cancelled in Rust vs timer.fired in C with the next checkpoint CANCELLED in Rust but OK in C (gen-1-21/28/30/48/52/74) - C misses a cancel; E/F) virtual time / completion order around driver cancel_task/cancel_region with Timeout/Deadline kinds and advance (gen-1-3/6/38/41/62/64/66/75). title: Child regions: Add asx_region_open_child() public API
description:
Add a new public API for opening a child region under a parent.

## API
asx_status asx_region_open_child(asx_region_id parent, asx_region_id *out_child);

## Semantics
1. Validate parent is alive and in OPEN state (via asx_region_slot_lookup + state check)
2. Validate parent's child_count < ASX_MAX_REGION_CHILDREN (return ASX_E_RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED if full)
3. Call existing asx_region_open(out_child) to allocate the child slot
4. Set child's parent_id = parent
5. Add child's id to parent's children[] array
6. Increment parent's child_count
7. Return ASX_OK

## Error conditions
- ASX_E_INVALID_ARGUMENT: null out_child
- ASX_E_NOT_FOUND: parent not found
- ASX_E_REGION_NOT_OPEN: parent not in OPEN state
- ASX_E_REGION_POISONED: parent is poisoned
- ASX_E_RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED: child slots full or no region slots available

## Files
- include/asx/runtime/runtime.h (add declaration)
- src/runtime/lifecycle.c (implement)

title: Budget-exhaustion cancels stay Cx-only until acknowledged (Rust); C writes them into the task record at once
description: Found by the differential fuzzer (bd-ij9w, seed 2, gen-2-91). In Rust a cancel raised by budget exhaustion (Cx::checkpoint's checkpoint_budget_exhaustion, cx.rs:2824-2836, and the lab's pre-poll quota check, lab/runtime.rs:4663-4670) only sets cancel_requested and the reason on the task's Cx. The TaskRecord stays Running until a checkpoint acknowledges the cancel and the scheduler reconciles it (TaskRecord::consume_checkpoint_cancel_ack, record/task.rs ~1171-1240). A task whose quota runs out inside a masked section and that then waits forever on a wait that is not cancel-aware (gen-2-91: poll_quota 2, sleep, masked checkpoint, notify_wait) therefore ends with record state Running, no cancel_reason and no cleanup_budget. C's asx_task_cancel_budget_internal moves the task to CANCEL_REQUESTED with the reason at once. Visible effects: (1) snapshot state/reason of such stuck tasks; (2) likely trace differences, because a later region cancel finds the Rust record still Running, so it counts as newly cancelled and records cancel.requested, while C only strengthens an existing cancel and records nothing. Fix sketch: keep a Cx-level pending budget cancel (reason, strengthened) beside the record state; asx_checkpoint reports it; an unmasked checkpoint materializes it into the record (request then acknowledge) as consume_checkpoint_cancel_ack does; region and direct cancels see an unmaterialized task as newly cancelled. Check what outcome a task that completes with an unacknowledged Cx cancel gets (Rust's spawn completion policies). Acceptance: gen-2-91 matches, a unit test for the masked case, and no regression in conformance or the fuzz batches.
close_reason: Implemented with unit tests; gen-2-91 and all 1466 fuzz scenarios match Rust

title: [Epic] Win32 Platform Adapter
description:
Replace the empty src/platform/win32/hooks.c stub with a real Win32 platform adapter that populates asx_runtime_hooks for live-mode Windows targets.

## Background
Same hook architecture as POSIX adapter (see POSIX epic for details on asx_runtime_hooks struct). Win32 uses different OS APIs: QueryPerformanceCounter for timing, BCryptGenRandom for entropy, WSAPoll or IOCP for reactor, CreateThread for blocking pool.

## Scope
Wave B/C. Lower priority than POSIX since the primary development environment is Linux.

## Deliverables
1. Clock hooks: QueryPerformanceCounter/QueryPerformanceFrequency for monotonic ns
2. Entropy hook: BCryptGenRandom from bcrypt.h
3. Reactor hook: WSAPoll or CreateIoCompletionPort wrapper
4. Blocking pool worker: CreateThread + event object for completion signaling
5. Export function: asx_win32_hooks_install(asx_runtime_hooks *h)
6. Public header: include/asx/platform/win32.h
7. Cross-compilation tests: verify compilation with mingw-w64 (no runtime execution)
8. Makefile: build-win32 target with conditional linking (-lbcrypt, -lws2_32)

## Files
- src/platform/win32/hooks.c (modify: replace empty stub)
- include/asx/platform/win32.h (new: public declaration)
- Makefile (modify: add build-win32 target)

title: EPIC: Production parallel runtime for 64-core agent swarms
description:
Idea-wizard output, 2026-05-08 (SilverFrog): create a production follow-on program for the current `ASX_PROFILE_PARALLEL` walking skeleton.

Context and non-duplication check:
- `bv --robot-triage` reports zero open/actionable/stalled beads; all prior work is closed.
- Prior closed beads such as `bd-2cw.7` and `bd-1eqo.4.2` implemented the optional parallel profile API shape and single-worker/lane simulation, not true live multi-threaded execution.
- `src/runtime/parallel.c` still states that it is a single-threaded simulation. `include/asx/runtime/parallel.h` caps workers at 4. `include/asx/platform/atomics.h` defaults to `ASX_LOCKFREE_SINGLE_THREAD=1`. POSIX detached blocking submit exists but is not wired into `asx_runtime_hooks`/`blocking.c`.

Goal:
Graduate parallel execution for massive agent-swarm deployments while preserving the project invariant that profiles alter resource/operational envelopes, not semantic behavior. The target is a runtime path that can exploit 64+ cores and 256GB+ RAM without nondeterministic semantic drift, silent drops, unbounded queues, or replay breakage.

Phase 2 top-five ideas selected:
1. Deterministic production parallel scheduler with work-stealing lanes and replay-stable commit ordering.
2. Portable atomics plus seqlock/EBR metadata graduation from research spikes.
3. Lock-free/two-phase MPSC channel graduation for high-contention agent messaging.
4. Hook-backed POSIX bounded worker/reactor integration instead of detached or ghost-only execution.
5. Parallel conformance, fuzz, and large-swarm e2e gates with structured JSONL logs.

Phase 3 next-ten ideas folded in:
NUMA/locality-aware arenas, large-swarm telemetry/admission control, sharded trace/replay logs, scheduler policy isomorphism, timed-lane/waker/reactor routing, 64-worker configuration surface, memory-model litmus/CBMC gates, RCH-backed benchmark baselines, deferred-stub graduation docs, and platform fallback contracts.

Acceptance:
This epic is complete only when every child task has unit tests, scenario/e2e or conformance proof as applicable, `rch exec -- make ...` validation evidence, and documentation updates for any deferred surface that graduates or remains deferred.

title: Define production parallel runtime contract and replay-stable success gates
description:
Define the binding contract for graduating `ASX_PROFILE_PARALLEL` from single-threaded simulation to production live-mode execution.

Must cover:
- Worker-count target and limits: support at least 64 logical workers without changing deterministic semantic outcomes.
- Semantic rule: parallel profile may alter throughput, scheduling mechanics, telemetry, and resource ceilings, but shared deterministic fixtures must retain identical canonical digests versus CORE/single-worker mode.
- Deterministic replay rule: workers may execute concurrently, but externally visible event ordering must be commit-ordered through a stable sequence authority.
- Fallback rule: CORE, FREESTANDING, EMBEDDED_ROUTER, HFT, AUTOMOTIVE, BROWSER, POSIX, and WIN32 must fail closed or use documented single-worker fallback when live workers are unavailable.
- Safety rule: no silent drops, no unbounded queues, no data races, and no allocator use after `asx_runtime_seal_allocator()` unless explicitly allowed by config.

- Add acceptance criteria mapping to Makefile gates and test suites.
- Include a non-duplication note that prior closed parallel beads implemented the API/simulation baseline, while this program graduates live-mode behavior.

title: EPIC: Rust Reference Fixture Capture Pipeline
description:
## Goal
Populate fixtures/rust_reference/ with golden outputs captured from the pinned Rust baseline
(commit 38c152405bd03e2bd9eecf178bfbbe9472fed861, toolchain nightly-2026-02-19).

## Why This Matters
The conformance gate currently runs against the C implementation's own fixtures, which validates
internal consistency but NOT Rust-vs-C behavioral parity. Without Rust-captured reference fixtures,
we cannot prove the C port produces identical semantic outputs for identical inputs. This is the
single highest-value remaining gap — it converts "self-consistent" into "provably equivalent."

## What "Done" Looks Like
- fixtures/rust_reference/ contains captured golden outputs for all 14 E2E fixture families (85+ scenarios)
- Each fixture has full provenance metadata (rust_baseline_commit, toolchain_commit_hash, cargo_lock_sha256)
- make conformance --fixtures-root fixtures/rust_reference passes with 0 semantic deltas
- Fixture schema validation passes against schemas/canonical_fixture.schema.json

## Architectural Context
The conformance infrastructure (tools/ci/run_conformance.sh) already supports --fixtures-root pointing
at Rust-captured data. The fixture schema, provenance map (docs/SOURCE_TO_FIXTURE_PROVENANCE_MAP.md,
28 provenance rows), and semantic delta budget policy (docs/SEMANTIC_DELTA_BUDGET.md, budget=0) are
all in place. This epic is purely about running the Rust side and capturing output.

## Risk
- The pinned Rust baseline may not build cleanly on current nightly (last verified 2026-02-26)
- Cargo.lock SHA must match exactly: 77f4bfaedfe5b8572dfca3181119f9432825ea3d868ee8f5d2793a6c5cdeffdc
- Any Rust-vs-C semantic delta discovered here would be a real bug (in either direction)
notes:
## IMPORTANT: FIXTURE DIRECTORY IS NOT EMPTY (2026-03-12 audit)

The fixtures/rust_reference/ directory IS populated with 7 families:
- smoke/ (10 fixtures), core_budget/, core_cancel/, core_channel/,
  core_lifecycle/, core_timer/, deployment_hardening/

HOWEVER, these are PLACEHOLDER/SCAFFOLD fixtures generated by the C implementation:
- semantic_digest values are "sha256:aaaaaaa..." (all-a placeholder)
- expected_events are empty arrays

  generated by actually running the Rust binary

The FEATURE_PARITY_VERIFICATION report (Gap #1) is correct: no actual Rust-generated
fixtures exist. The directory contains structural scaffolds.

## What This Epic Does
Replace placeholder fixtures with REAL Rust-generated golden outputs by:
1. Setting up Rust build environment
2. Building the Rust binary in fixture capture mode
3. Running it to generate real fixtures (replacing placeholders)
4. Validating the real fixtures against the schema
5. Running C conformance against real Rust fixtures (first true parity test)
6. E2E test verifying the entire pipeline

## Dependency Structure
Linear: .1 → .2 → .3 → .4 → .5, then .6 (e2e test) depends on .5

title: Set up Rust baseline build environment
description:
## Goal
Install the exact pinned Rust toolchain and check out the pinned baseline commit so that
the Rust reference implementation can be built reproducibly.

## Detailed Steps
1. Install rustup if not present
2. Install exact toolchain: nightly-2026-02-19 (compiler hash 7f99507f57e6c4aa0dce3daf6a13cca8cd4dd312)
3. Clone or fetch https://github.com/Dicklesworthstone/asupersync

6. Run cargo build --release to verify the baseline compiles
7. Run cargo test --release to verify the baseline's own tests pass

## Why This Specific Pinning
The entire conformance infrastructure is built around this exact commit and toolchain.
The provenance fields in every fixture (rust_baseline_commit, rust_toolchain_commit_hash,
cargo_lock_sha256) must match exactly, or the conformance runner will reject fixtures as
having mismatched provenance. See docs/RUST_BASELINE_PROVENANCE.md for the dual-baseline
rebase protocol.

## Acceptance Criteria
- cargo build --release succeeds on the pinned commit with the pinned toolchain
- cargo test --release passes with zero failures
- Cargo.lock SHA matches the documented value
- rustc --version reports the expected nightly version

## Testing

- Verify: rustc +nightly-2026-02-19 --version prints expected output
- Verify: cargo test --release 2>&1 | tail -5 shows "test result: ok"
- Document: number of passing tests in Rust baseline (for future reference)

## Why cargo test Matters
If the Rust baseline's own tests fail on the pinned commit, it means either the commit
is broken or the toolchain version is wrong. This is a pre-condition for generating
trustworthy reference fixtures.

title: Build Rust reference binary with fixture capture mode
description:
## Goal
Build the Rust asupersync binary in a mode that can execute scenario fixtures and emit
canonical output in the fixture schema format.

## Context
The Rust implementation needs to be invoked as a fixture runner — given scenario inputs
(seed, region/task/obligation setup, scheduler ticks), it should produce:
- Trace events (ordered, with entity_id and aux)
- Final snapshot (region/task/obligation states)
- Semantic digest (FNV-1a hash chain)
- Error codes for negative/must-fail scenarios

The output must conform to schemas/canonical_fixture.schema.json with full provenance fields.

## Detailed Steps
1. **Explore the Rust codebase** to find existing test/benchmark infrastructure:
   - Check for integration test binaries in tests/ or benches/
   - Look for snapshot/fixture capture code
   - Check if there's a CLI entry point that runs scenarios
   - Audit Cargo.toml for binary targets beyond the library

2. If a fixture runner exists: adapt its output to match our fixture schema
3. If NO fixture runner exists: create a thin Rust binary (tools/fixture_capture/src/main.rs):
   - Reads scenario definition JSON from stdin or --scenario flag
   - Instantiates the Rust runtime with deterministic mode
   - Executes the scenario (region ops, task spawns, scheduler ticks)
   - Collects trace events and final state
   - Emits fixture JSON to stdout
   - Populates provenance fields from the build environment

4. Build with --release for deterministic behavior
5. Verify output validates against the fixture schema
6. Test with at least 3 scenarios from different families

## RISK: Fixture Runner May Need Creation
The Rust baseline may not have a ready-made fixture runner. If creation is needed,
the work involves:
- Understanding Rust asupersync's public API surface (region, task, scheduler)
- Writing a scenario interpreter that maps our fixture schema's inputs to Rust API calls
- Collecting trace events and computing digests in the same format as the C side

If this is the case, the estimate may need to increase from 120m to 240m. The
implementing agent should assess within the first 30m and flag if the estimate
needs revision.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Rust binary accepts scenario input and produces fixture JSON output
- Output validates against schemas/canonical_fixture.schema.json
- Provenance fields populated correctly from build environment
- At least 3 scenarios from different families produce non-trivial output

## Testing
- Run: ./fixture_capture --scenario smoke/profile_core.json | jq .
- Verify: output contains non-empty expected_events array
- Verify: semantic_digest is a real SHA256, not a placeholder
- Verify: check-jsonschema validates output against canonical schema
- Verify: running the same scenario twice produces identical output (determinism)

title: Validate captured fixtures against canonical schema
description:
## Goal
Run schema validation on every captured Rust fixture to ensure they conform to
schemas/canonical_fixture.schema.json before using them as conformance baselines.

## Why Validation Before Use
A malformed fixture that slips into the reference set would cause false conformance failures
or, worse, false passes (if the C runner also produces the same malformation). Schema validation
catches structural issues before they become semantic ghosts.

## Detailed Steps
1. Use a JSON schema validator (jsonschema CLI, Python jsonschema, or a C validator)
2. Validate every file in fixtures/rust_reference/**/*.json against canonical_fixture.schema.json
3. Check provenance fields are non-empty and match pinned values:
   - rust_baseline_commit == 38c152405bd03e2bd9eecf178bfbbe9472fed861
   - rust_toolchain_commit_hash == 7f99507f57e6c4aa0dce3daf6a13cca8cd4dd312
   - cargo_lock_sha256 == 77f4bfaedfe5b8572dfca3181119f9432825ea3d868ee8f5d2793a6c5cdeffdc
4. Check semantic_digest fields are NOT placeholder (no sha256:aaa... values)
5. Check expected_events arrays are non-empty for positive scenarios
6. Report any validation failures with file path and violation details
7. Create tools/ci/validate_fixtures.sh that wraps the above as a reusable script

## JSONL Output Format
{"ts":"...","fixture":"smoke/profile_core.codec_json.json","status":"pass","checks":["schema","provenance","digest_real","events_present"]}
{"ts":"...","fixture":"core_budget/BUDGET-001.json","status":"fail","check":"digest_real","detail":"contains placeholder sha256:aaa..."}
{"ts":"...","summary":"validation_complete","total":87,"passed":87,"failed":0,"duration_ms":1200}

## Testing
1. Create tests/ci/test_validate_fixtures.sh that validates the validation script itself:
   a. Create a temp directory with 3 fixture types:
      - valid_fixture.json (passes all checks)
      - bad_schema.json (missing required field)
      - placeholder_digest.json (contains sha256:aaa...)
   b. Run validate_fixtures.sh against the temp directory
   c. Verify: valid passes, bad_schema fails with "schema" reason, placeholder fails with "digest_real" reason
   d. Verify: JSONL output is parseable by jq
   e. Verify: exit code is non-zero when any fixture fails

2. Test the provenance check specifically:
   a. Create fixture with wrong rust_baseline_commit
   b. Verify validate_fixtures.sh catches it

## Acceptance Criteria
- 100% of fixtures pass schema validation
- Zero provenance field mismatches
- Zero placeholder digests remaining
- validate_fixtures.sh is reusable for future baseline rebases
- JSONL output per-fixture with summary line
- Companion test script validates the validation logic itself

title: Run C conformance against Rust reference fixtures (first Rust-vs-C parity run)
description:
## Goal
Execute the definitive Rust-vs-C parity check: run make conformance with --fixtures-root
pointing at the newly-captured Rust reference fixtures.

## Why This Is The Most Important Task In The Epic
This is the moment of truth. Every prior task was setup for this: does the C port produce
semantically identical outputs to the Rust reference for every scenario? A pass here
means provably equivalent behavior. A failure means we have real divergence to investigate.

## Detailed Steps
1. Run: tools/ci/run_conformance.sh --mode conformance --fixtures-root fixtures/rust_reference
2. Capture the conformance report (JSONL + summary JSON + semantic delta artifact)
3. If semantic_delta_count == 0: full parity confirmed
4. If semantic_delta_count > 0: for each delta, classify per SEMANTIC_DELTA_BUDGET.md taxonomy:
   - none: no real delta (harness artifact)
   - intentional_upstream: Rust behavior we intentionally diverge from (requires written ruling)
   - c_regression: bug in C port (must fix)
   - spec_defect: ambiguity in the spec (requires written ruling)
   - harness_defect: bug in the test harness (must fix)
5. Any c_regression deltas become new beads with priority 0
6. Update docs/FEATURE_PARITY.md with results

## Semantic Delta Budget Policy
The budget is 0 (docs/SEMANTIC_DELTA_BUDGET.md). Any non-zero delta count requires explicit
classification, root-cause analysis, and sign-off before the gate can pass. This is by design:
we want zero tolerance for undocumented behavioral differences.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Conformance run completes without infrastructure errors
- semantic_delta_count == 0 (ideal) OR all deltas are classified and approved
- Conformance artifact archived in tools/ci/artifacts/conformance/
- docs/FEATURE_PARITY.md updated to reflect Rust-vs-C parity status

title: E2E test script for Rust fixture pipeline with structured JSONL logging
description:
## Context
The Rust fixture capture pipeline (bd-reg6.1 through bd-reg6.5) is a multi-step
workflow where each step depends on the previous. If any step fails silently or
produces subtly wrong output, downstream steps may pass incorrectly. We need an
end-to-end test that validates the entire pipeline and provides detailed logging
for debugging failures.

## Background
The pipeline steps are:
1. Rust toolchain setup (bd-reg6.1)
2. Rust binary build (bd-reg6.2)
3. Fixture capture for all families (bd-reg6.3)
4. Schema validation of captured fixtures (bd-reg6.4)
5. C-vs-Rust conformance run (bd-reg6.5)

Each step has its own acceptance criteria, but there's no single test that
validates the pipeline end-to-end. A pipeline e2e test catches integration bugs.

## Task
1. Create tools/ci/test_fixture_pipeline_e2e.sh that:
   a. Runs the complete pipeline from Rust setup through conformance
   b. Validates every intermediate artifact exists and is non-empty
   c. Checks provenance consistency across all fixtures
   d. Verifies fixture count matches expectations per family
   e. Runs the conformance check and captures the full report
   f. Produces structured JSONL log output to stdout

2. JSONL Log Format (one JSON object per line):
   {"ts":"...","step":"rust_setup","status":"pass","detail":"nightly-2026-02-19 installed","duration_ms":4523}
   {"ts":"...","step":"rust_build","status":"pass","detail":"release binary 14.2MB","duration_ms":62100}
   {"ts":"...","step":"fixture_capture","status":"pass","detail":"87 fixtures in 14 families","duration_ms":31200}
   {"ts":"...","step":"schema_validation","status":"pass","detail":"87/87 valid","duration_ms":800}
   {"ts":"...","step":"provenance_check","status":"pass","detail":"all provenance fields match","duration_ms":200}
   {"ts":"...","step":"conformance_run","status":"pass","detail":"66 records, 0 deltas","duration_ms":5400}
   {"ts":"...","step":"pipeline_result","status":"pass","detail":"full pipeline green","duration_ms":104223}

3. On failure, log specific error with full context including fixture path and violation.

4. Create companion unit test (tests/ci/test_pipeline_e2e_test.sh) that validates
   the e2e script itself using mock artifacts (no Rust toolchain required):
   - Mock a minimal fixture set
   - Verify script correctly detects missing fixtures
   - Verify script correctly detects provenance mismatches
   - Verify JSONL output is parseable by jq

## Acceptance Criteria
- E2E script runs full pipeline and exits 0 when all steps pass
- E2E script exits 1 and logs the failing step when any step fails
- All log output is valid JSONL
- Companion test validates script behavior without Rust toolchain
- Script is idempotent (safe to re-run)

## Why This Matters
Without an e2e test, pipeline failures are diagnosed by manually running each step.
Structured JSONL logging enables automated triage: pipe to jq to find the failing
step. Especially valuable in CI.

title: EPIC: Differential Fuzzing Parity Gate (GATE-FUZZ)
description:
## Goal
Implement GATE-FUZZ: differential fuzzing that runs the same randomized inputs through both the
Rust reference implementation and the C port, comparing outputs for semantic equivalence.

## Why This Matters
Unit tests and conformance fixtures cover known scenarios. Differential fuzzing discovers UNKNOWN
divergences — edge cases where the C port's behavior differs from Rust under unusual input
combinations. This is the gold standard for porting correctness: if a fuzzer can't find a
difference after millions of iterations, confidence in behavioral equivalence is very high.

GATE-FUZZ is one of the 9 non-negotiable quality gates defined in AGENTS.md (lines 249-259):
"Differential fuzzing gate (Rust vs C + minimized counterexamples)."

## What "Done" Looks Like
- Fuzz harnesses exist for all major subsystems (lifecycle, channel, timer, scheduler, codec)
- A differential driver feeds identical inputs to Rust and C, compares outputs
- Counterexample minimization pipeline reduces failing inputs to minimal reproducers
- make fuzz-parity runs a smoke campaign (bounded iterations) that passes
- CI integration via the fuzz-parity blocking gate

## Architectural Context
The deterministic mode (ASX_DETERMINISTIC=1) ensures that for identical inputs and seeds,
both implementations should produce byte-identical trace digests. The trace digest (FNV-1a
hash chain) is the primary comparison point. The existing asx_trace_digest() and
asx_hindsight_digest() functions provide the comparison surface.

## Dependencies
Requires the Rust reference fixture capture pipeline (Epic 1) to be functional, since the
differential driver needs to invoke both the Rust binary and the C binary.

## Risk
- Requires building and running Rust and C in the same pipeline
- Fuzz campaigns are compute-intensive; CI time budget must be bounded
- Any found divergence requires root-cause analysis and classification per SEMANTIC_DELTA_BUDGET.md
notes:
## CRITICAL: EXISTING INFRASTRUCTURE AUDIT (2026-03-12)

The following ALREADY EXISTS and must NOT be recreated:
- tests/fuzz/fuzz_differential.c: Complete 1149-line differential fuzz harness (bd-1md.3)
  - 21 op types, xoshiro256** PRNG, FNV-1a digest, mutation engine, JSONL reporting
  - CLI: --seed, --iterations, --smoke, --nightly, --fixtures-dir, --verbose
- tests/fuzz/fuzz_minimize.c: Complete 1080-line minimizer (bd-1md.4)
  - Delta debugging, single-op removal, arg simplification, 3 self-tests
- Makefile targets: fuzz-build, fuzz-smoke, fuzz-run, fuzz-nightly
- make check-ci already includes fuzz-smoke

## DEPENDENCY STRUCTURE (revised 2026-03-12 pass 5)
C-side work (rkql.1, .2, .8) does NOT depend on Rust baseline. Only rkql.3 depends
on bd-reg6.1 (Rust build env). This allows C-side audit/hardening to proceed in
PARALLEL with Epic 1 Rust setup.

Three parallel entry points (no serial bottleneck):
  Track A (code review):  rkql.1 → rkql.2 ──────────→ rkql.6 → rkql.4 → rkql.5 → rkql.7
  Track B (Rust-side):    reg6.1 → rkql.3 ──────────→ rkql.6 (joins Track A)
  Track C (execution):    rkql.8 (sanitizer validation, fully independent)

IMPORTANT: rkql.2 (code review) and rkql.8 (sanitizer execution) are SEPARATE concerns.
rkql.2 reads and analyzes code — it does NOT run the harness.
rkql.8 runs the harness under sanitizers — it does NOT review code structure.
There is NO overlap between these two beads.

## Subtask Inventory (8 total, 780m)
.1 Audit/document existing grammar (60m)
.2 Code review of existing C harness (90m) — reading only, no execution
.3 Implement Rust-side fuzz target (180m — genuinely new)
.4 Extend fuzz_differential.c for live Rust comparison (120m)
.5 Audit/integrate existing minimizer (60m)
.6 Cross-language grammar determinism tests (120m)
.7 Extend CI gate for Rust comparison (90m)
.8 ASan/UBSan execution validation (60m — independent track)

title: Audit existing C fuzz harness for completeness and correctness
description:
## STATUS: EXISTING IMPLEMENTATION — CODE REVIEW AND GAP ANALYSIS

## Context
A comprehensive fuzz harness ALREADY EXISTS:
- tests/fuzz/fuzz_differential.c (1149 lines, 21 op types)
- tests/fuzz/fuzz_minimize.c (1080 lines, 3 strategies)
This bead is a CODE REVIEW — read and analyze, do not execute. Execution-based
validation (sanitizers, determinism) is handled separately by bd-rkql.8.

## What ACTUALLY Needs To Be Done
1. **Grammar completeness audit** (cross-reference with rkql.1 docs):
   - Do all 21 FUZZ_OP types exercise meaningful runtime behavior?
   - Are weight biases (OP_WEIGHTS) appropriate? Over-represented ops waste iterations.
   - Check: cancel_kind coverage (currently op->arg_u32 % 11u — are all 11 cancel kinds valid?)
   - Check: channel backpressure scenarios — does the grammar create full-channel situations?
   - Check: are profile-specific code paths exercised? (FREESTANDING, EMBEDDED_ROUTER)

2. **Handle tracking correctness review**:
   - Does the harness properly handle slot exhaustion (all region/task/channel slots full)?
   - Are handle reuse races possible? (close region, reopen, use stale handle)
   - Review sim_time advancement: is timer interaction realistic?
   - Review channel permit lifecycle: reserve→send vs reserve→abort, all paths covered?

3. **Mutation engine review**:
   - Are all 7 mutation operators meaningful? (remove, duplicate, swap, change_kind, tweak_arg, insert, change_idx)
   - Can any mutation produce invalid scenarios? (e.g., negative array index)
   - Review bounds checking on idx_a, idx_b, arg_u32, arg_u64

4. **Digest computation review**:
   - Is the FNV-1a hash chain order deterministic across platforms?
   - Are all semantically-relevant outputs included in the digest?
   - Are any semantically-irrelevant outputs (timing, allocation addresses) accidentally included?

5. **Document findings** as concrete items:
   - Bugs found → new P0 beads
   - Missing coverage → additions for rkql.4 or follow-up beads
   - Design concerns → documented in FUZZ_PARITY_DESIGN.md (from rkql.1)

## What This Bead Does NOT Do
- Does NOT run the harness (that is bd-rkql.8)
- Does NOT run sanitizers (that is bd-rkql.8)
- Does NOT modify the code unless a clear bug is found during review

## Acceptance Criteria
- All 21 op types reviewed for semantic coverage — documented checklist
- Handle tracking logic reviewed — no out-of-bounds or use-after-free patterns
- Mutation engine reviewed — all operators produce valid transformations
- Digest computation reviewed — confirmed deterministic and semantically complete
- Findings documented: count of bugs, gaps, and design concerns
- Any bugs found filed as new beads with P0 priority

## Why Separate From rkql.8
Code review (reading + reasoning) and execution testing (running + measuring) are
different skills that can be parallelized. An agent can review the code structure
while another agent runs it under sanitizers. Combining them in one bead creates
a serial bottleneck.

title: Implement Rust-side fuzz target using same input grammar
description:
## Context
The C-side fuzz harness (tests/fuzz/fuzz_differential.c) already has a --fixtures-dir
flag for comparing against Rust reference outputs, but the Rust-side fuzz target
that accepts the SAME input grammar and produces comparable digests does not exist yet.

## Background
The existing C harness uses a grammar with 21 operation types, xoshiro256** PRNG,
and FNV-1a digest computation. The Rust target must replicate ALL of these:
- Same PRNG (xoshiro256** with splitmix64 seeding) — byte-exact
- Same scenario generation from seed
- Same FNV-1a hash chain over operation results and scheduler events
- Same digest output format (uint64 hex)

The grammar specification is documented in docs/FUZZ_PARITY_DESIGN.md (from bd-rkql.1).

## Key Requirement: Byte-Exact Reproducibility
Given the SAME seed, the Rust target must:
1. Generate the SAME scenario (same ops in same order with same args)
2. Execute against the Rust asupersync runtime
3. Produce a digest — this digest may DIFFER from C (different runtime behavior)
   but the input interpretation must be IDENTICAL

The differential comparison is: same input → different digest = behavioral divergence.
NOT: same input → different input interpretation = infrastructure bug.

## Task
1. Implement Rust fuzz target at e.g. tools/fuzz/rust_fuzz_target/src/main.rs:
   - Port xoshiro256** PRNG (byte-exact with C version)
   - Port scenario generation with identical op type mapping
   - Execute scenarios against Rust asupersync runtime
   - Compute FNV-1a digest over results and events
   - Output single-line hex digest to stdout

2. Create integration test: run C and Rust with same seed, parse scenario only
   (no execution), verify identical operation sequences

3. Wire into fuzz_differential.c's --fixtures-dir mode: Rust target pre-generates
   fixtures, C harness compares against them

## Acceptance Criteria
- Rust target compiles against pinned baseline
- Same seed → same scenario (verified by comparing op sequences without execution)
- Digest output format matches C (16-char hex uint64)
- At least 100 seeds produce matching scenario interpretations

## Existing Infrastructure To Build On
- fuzz_differential.c already has --fixtures-dir flag (unused until Rust fixtures exist)
- schemas/canonical_fixture.schema.json defines the fixture format
- docs/FUZZ_PARITY_DESIGN.md (from bd-rkql.1) documents the grammar

## Why This Is Still Manual Work
The Rust side is genuinely new code — no existing implementation. However, it's
a PORT of the C grammar, not a design exercise, so it's more mechanical.

title: Extend fuzz_differential.c with --rust-binary live comparison mode
description:
## STATUS: PARTIALLY EXISTS — EXTEND EXISTING HARNESS

## Context
The existing fuzz_differential.c already has a --fixtures-dir flag for comparing
against pre-generated reference outputs. However, it currently only does:
1. Determinism self-check (run same scenario twice, compare C-vs-C digest)
2. Mutation + crash detection

It does NOT yet support live Rust binary comparison (run Rust target in real-time).

## What ACTUALLY Needs To Be Done
Extend fuzz_differential.c to support a new comparison mode: --rust-binary <path>

### Mode 1: Fixture-based comparison (existing --fixtures-dir)
- Pre-generate Rust reference digests using the Rust target (bd-rkql.3)
- C harness reads pre-computed Rust digests from fixture files
- Compare C digest vs stored Rust digest for each seed
- This is FAST (no Rust process per iteration) but requires fixture regeneration

### Mode 2: Live comparison (new --rust-binary <path>)
- For each scenario, serialize seed to temp file or pipe
- Invoke Rust binary with that seed
- Capture Rust digest from stdout
- Compare with C digest
- This is SLOWER but always uses current Rust code

### Implementation Plan
1. Add --rust-binary <path> CLI flag to fuzz_differential.c
2. After computing C digest, fork+exec Rust binary with same seed
3. Capture Rust digest from stdout, parse hex
4. Compare: if C_digest != Rust_digest → log divergence with full JSONL detail
5. Add a --batch mode for efficiency: generate N seeds, run Rust once with all seeds

## Testing
1. Unit test: mock Rust binary that always returns a known digest
   - tests/fuzz/test_differential_rust_mode.sh
   - Create a tiny C program that echoes a fixed digest
   - Run fuzz_differential --rust-binary ./mock_binary --iterations 10
   - Verify: if mock returns same digest as C → pass; different → logged divergence
2. Integration test: use real Rust binary (requires rkql.3)
   - Run 100 seeds, verify cross-language grammar match (from rkql.6)
   - Then run full differential comparison
3. JSONL log validation: pipe output through jq, verify all fields present

## Acceptance Criteria
- fuzz_differential --rust-binary ./rust_fuzz_target --iterations 1000 works
- Divergences logged with JSONL including both digests and full op sequence
- Batch mode achieves >100 comparisons/second
- Mock-based test passes without Rust toolchain
- No divergences found on 1000 iterations (if parity is correct)

## What Already Works (don't touch)
- Scenario generation and mutation engine
- C-side execution and digest computation
- JSONL reporting infrastructure
- --smoke and --nightly iteration modes

## Estimate
120m (extending existing code, not building from scratch).

title: Oracle blind spot: group members and child regions refused while their region closes (38/2000 fuzz scenarios uncapturable)
description:
## Problem
In fuzz seeds 1-20 x100 (2026-10-09), twin_run could not capture 38 of 2000 generated scenarios, so the Rust-vs-C comparison never sees them:
- 30: 'spawned task ... was never admitted'. A task-group member (join_all, quorum, first_ok) is spawned into a region already cancelled or closing. Rust's spawn mailbox accepts it and the next step's admission refuses it (runtime/state.rs:1702). twin_run's project_denied_spawns only handles plain spawn steps; a combinator's member has no raw outcome, so it is reported as a harness defect.
- 8: 'unknown child region' / 'spawn into unknown region'. A step uses a child region whose open_region failed (the DSL §3 not-held rule is not applied to child regions in twin_run).
C cannot express the first class either: interpreter.c spawn_group_members fails the run when asx_task_group_spawn returns ASX_E_REGION_CLOSED.

## Rust semantics to reproduce
- A refused member's join resolves only when the next step's admission refuses it, as JoinError::Cancelled(closed_reason()). The reason is the Cx/abort reason if any, else CancelReason::user("join channel closed") (task_handle.rs:1016-1023).
- That resolution wakes the owner's join registration at the registered priority. C already models this for plain spawns: asx_scheduler_last_spawn_refusal, asx_task_await_refusal, refusal records in the lab admission FIFO.
- Per combinator:
  - join_all lists the member as cancelled;
  - quorum counts a failure (QuorumFailure::Cancelled);
  - first_ok's attempt ends cancelled.
  Check scope.rs for each (join_all :1479, quorum :1811-1941, first_ok :2023-2099).

## Work
1. twin_run: in project_denied_spawns, accept group members (s.group_members). Then project child-region not-held steps as ASX_E_NOT_FOUND, as the C interpreter does.
2. C: let asx_task_group_spawn/add_attempt take a refused member, completed as CANCELLED with the 'join channel closed' reason and visible to the group only once its refusal is delivered. Let the interpreter keep running.
3. Re-run make fuzz-differential over seeds 1-20 and minimize any FAIL.

## Done when
twin_run captures these classes, C matches them, and the uncapturable share of a 20-seed run is near zero.

## Credit rules
Real tests; the Rust oracle decides; never edit fixtures.
close_reason: Done: both classes capture and match under the Rust oracle (65/65; seeds 41-60: 0/2000 uncapturable)
